title: What If Avoiding AI Is the Real Risk?
author: Joel Salinas
summary: Salinas and co-author Jose Antonio Morales argue that leaders who wait out AI are not being cautious but are abdicating. They compare AI avoidance to earlier leaders who dismissed websites, social media and online giving, and they claim inaction signals unwillingness to adapt. The case rests on three points: avoidance risks irrelevance, small organisations such as nonprofits and church teams stand to gain the most from AI's leverage, and fear-based leadership misses the chance to shape how the tool is used. They answer common myths (too small, unethical, wait for others) and call for wise integration with clear boundaries and values rather than blind adoption. The piece is aimed at mission-driven leaders and stays at the level of exhortation, with few concrete examples or evidence beyond analogy.
points: Waiting is defensible only if it is active learning, and passive waiting is recast as a leadership failure.
Small organisations gain the most because AI substitutes for staff, budget and specialist skills they lack.
The historical analogy to leaders who rejected websites and social media is used to argue that late adopters lose relevance.
Disengaging removes a leader's voice from the choices about how AI is used, so values are best protected by engaging with boundaries.
quotes: Avoiding AI may seem wise, even the right thing to do. But in a rapidly changing landscape, inaction becomes its own form of leadership failure. It tells your team (and the world) that you’re unwilling to adapt. That you’d rather protect comfort than pursue clarity.
You don’t have to adopt every tool. But refusing to engage at all? That’s not caution. That’s abdication.
The very leaders who fear AI the most, nonprofits, church teams, scrappy startups, are the ones AI could actually help the most. Why? Because AI levels the playing field.
It comes from building learning cultures. From experimenting in small, safe ways. Letting go of perfectionism and embracing progress.
Every powerful technology comes with real misuse. But the solution isn’t rejection, it’s wise integration.
Avoiding AI entirely doesn’t protect your values. It just removes your voice from shaping how it’s used.
You don’t need to master the mechanics. But you do need to stay awake to what’s changing, and to what must remain human.
